title: Active management graduation rule becomes risk-adjusted: an in-trade action class passes if it gives up <= a pre-stated R/trade (0.05R proposed) while cutting book max drawdown or worst-5% outcome materially (>=15%), across folds, vs a random-intervention control, measured on the whole book; then pre-register the break-even-stop-after-peak test on the real-money legs under it
note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-10-29 ~06:25Z (popup, verbatim answer): "Small R cost for big risk cut (Recommended)". Option text shown: 'Passes if it gives up at most a set amount of R per trade (I'd propose 0.05R, fixed before the run) while cutting the book's max drawdown or worst 5% of outcomes materially (e.g. 15%+). Must hold across time periods and beat a random-intervention control, measured on the whole book.' Operator reasoning, verbatim: "if we've gotten to a place where we can still find ourselves getting reward while zeroing out the risk of the trade, then that seems to me like it's a better trading decision overall than to keep on time and time again just giving back all of the gains." Supersedes the 'judged against hold' (mean net R) wording of docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md § Active management clause 4 for graduation. Unchanged: each class graduates on its OWN registered test; net of the full cost stack; rule registered before the run; Tier-3/mandate path to execute; two gates; TP doctrine. Motivating case: ADA-AM-CASE (break-even stop: EV cost 0.01-0.03R, worst -1.04R -> -0.17R, sub-floor n=19). [2026-10-29 ~06:35Z] OPERATOR, verbatim (generalises the rule into the system's objective): "This is an issue of metrics, not an issue of the trade itself ... If nothing else, reducing risk is always the second most important thing. So if everything else is even, then reducing risk is the right decision to make. And reducing lots of risk for a small cost in R is also the right decision to make ... the long-term P&L isn't just one trade. It's our ability to manage risk over time. And if we're not managing our risk because we're trying to get, you know, 0.5 more R or whatever, then we're obviously not going to make money in the long run." Reading: the objective is LEXICOGRAPHIC with a trade-off: (1) net P&L; (2) risk reduction as the tie-breaker; and a large risk cut for a small R cost is preferred. State it ONCE as the objective (ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL § Active management + OPERATING-PLAN § 2, or wherever the doc hierarchy says the objective lives) and point at it. [2026-10-29 ~06:40Z, Thursday planning] OPERATOR: "For the first one, yes, agree". Perf-review call D2 (giveback rise; pipeline PI-20261028-PVRNY2JI-0002) is folded into active management and graded under RULE-AM-RISK-ADJUSTED-V1, not a separate /perf-followup track. Disposition (a) for the planning close PR. [2026-10-29 ~07:10Z] OPERATOR, verbatim (sharpens the objective): "We've been measuring R, which is a good measure, and we need to continue that. But the main goal isn't most R as much as it's most overall P&L, right? We need to measure P&L and percentage on an absolute numbers because we're working with small accounts and different accounts of different sizes. But the what we care about is return, not necessarily just return for risk. We do care about R, which is why we also want to reduce risk when reducing risk will have a small impact on reward. But what we care about here is the overall amount of money that we make, not the overall amount of money we make necessarily in relation to the amount of risk that was taken." Reading: PRIMARY = absolute net P&L, reported in $ and % return per account (and book); R remains the per-trade unit of measure; risk reduction is the tie-breaker and wins when its reward cost is small; risk-adjusted ratios (Sharpe, return/DD) are NOT the objective. [2026-10-29 ~07:20Z] OPERATOR, verbatim: "if we're optimizing for R, then that also matters how much risk we're taking. But like, this is why banking makes sense, because it might not be the best R trade-off, but it will make the most money overall and for each trade." MANAGER (stated to the operator): per trade at fixed risk, $ = R x risk, and banking at +2R on ada lost -9..-18R (b7e1-08), so 'more money per trade' is not what the data shows. Banking can make more money OVERALL only via book-level effects a per-trade test cannot see: (1) freed risk budget lets the book take trades the risk caps would refuse (pays only when caps bind); (2) compounding under %-of-equity sizing after smaller drawdowns; (3) prop account survival vs daily DD limits. REQUIREMENT for the rule: grade on a BOOK-LEVEL $ simulation per account at its real size, with the production sizer and risk caps (concurrency, per-account caps, daily DD switch), so all three effects are counted. R stays the per-trade unit. [2026-10-29 ~07:05Z lane, third addendum] Clause 4 now names the measurement of record: a book-level $ simulation per account at real size, using the production sizer and caps (concurrency, per-account caps, daily_dd_switch). R1 is delta net $ and % return, with R per trade beside it; R2 is drawdown / CVaR in $ and %. MEASURED gap: no harness does this. backtest_system.py is one book on one symbol with a mirrored sizer, nbook_portfolio.py is N books over one stream, and neither has daily_dd_switch or --be-floor-r. Filed as row BOOK-SIM-REAL-SIZER, the first gap. The grader now labels R-book grades measurement_basis=per_trade_r_screen, graduation_eligible=false. The re-grade above is that screen. RQ-20261029-1f39-01 is blocked on both rows.
